scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: The design is broadly coherent for large-scale web search, with strong crawl/index separation, generation-aware serving, locale-aware analysis, and ranked query flow, but the multi-modal content requirement is only partially expressed.

findings.title: Media support is mostly text-derived rather than a fully explicit multi-modal search path
findings.explanation: The design clearly extracts OCR, captions, transcripts, and content-type metadata, which is enough to support search over text associated with images and videos. However, the query and ranking flow does not explicitly show a dedicated retrieval or result presentation path for image/video search beyond safe media references, so the core requirement is only partially covered.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit media-search branch or result mode that can retrieve and rank image/video entities directly, while still using extracted text signals for relevance.

findings.title: Generation-bound caching and deadline propagation support fast first-page search
findings.explanation: The request path uses a generation-aware cache keyed by locale and filters, and the coordinator propagates absolute deadlines through analyzer, index, and ranker calls. This is a strong fit for the 200ms search objective.

results.summary: The architecture covers the legacy notification scope well: multi-channel delivery, preference enforcement, versioned templates, retries, analytics, rate limiting, and spike handling are all represented with coherent component boundaries and flows.

findings.title: Channel isolation and retries are coherently decomposed
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates command intake, policy/orchestration, per-channel queues, delivery workers, provider adapters, and a DLQ, which makes failure handling and channel-specific scaling easy to reason about.

findings.title: Consistent privacy posture across storage and analytics
findings.explanation: Sensitive recipient data is kept opaque or encrypted, and analytics explicitly excludes raw addresses, device tokens, IPs, and message bodies. This is a strong fit for the privacy constraint.

results.summary: The design covers the core distributed file-storage scope with resumable chunked transfers, authoritative ACL enforcement, versioned metadata, offline sync, searchable content, and explicit durability/backup paths.

findings.title: Offline conflict handling is preserved instead of overwritten
findings.explanation: Clients carry base revision context, replay idempotent edits after reconnect, and the metadata store keeps conflict versions rather than silently applying last-writer-wins. This directly supports offline edits while protecting concurrent changes.

findings.title: Permission checks are anchored to authoritative metadata
findings.explanation: The file API resolves owner, inherited grants, explicit ACLs, and revocations server-side before reads, writes, search-result disclosure, or URL issuance, which keeps authorization independent of client state.

findings.title: Upload pipeline protects large files from partial visibility
findings.explanation: Uploads use resumable sessions and only publish complete manifests after checksum validation and conditional metadata commit, so a 1GB file is not exposed as a half-finished object.

results.summary: The design covers paste creation, short unique URLs, aliases, expiry, syntax highlighting, view counting, and read-heavy scaling with coherent cache, queue, and cleanup paths.

findings.title: Asynchronous view counting preserves read-path latency
findings.explanation: Successful GETs are captured at the edge and processed through a durable queue and worker path, so analytics do not add synchronous writes to paste retrieval.

findings.title: Expiry handling is fenced before cleanup
findings.explanation: The metadata store rejects reads at expiry, while workers tombstone and retry deletion idempotently, preventing delayed cleanup from extending paste lifetime.

findings.title: Short-code generation avoids centralized counters
findings.explanation: The key generator produces compact base36 candidates and the metadata database is the authority for conditional reservation, which supports uniqueness without a global incrementing bottleneck.

results.summary: The design covers the full Instagram core scope with coherent service boundaries for uploads, social graph, feed, stories, search, messaging, and notifications, while also addressing celebrity-scale feed handling and media delivery efficiency.

findings.title: Hybrid feed strategy addresses celebrity-scale fan-out
findings.explanation: The feed service explicitly combines fan-out-on-write for ordinary authors with fan-out-on-read for celebrity accounts, which is the key architectural choice needed to keep feed generation viable at the required follower counts.

findings.title: Media delivery is decoupled from upload and processing
findings.explanation: Uploads go directly to object storage, processing is offloaded to workers, and reads are served through the CDN. That separation supports availability for uploads and keeps large media bodies off application servers.

findings.title: Real-time notification path is event-driven
findings.explanation: Committed follow, interaction, story, and message events are carried through the broker to a dedicated notification service, which is a clean basis for asynchronous, user-scoped push delivery.

results.summary: The design covers the full autocomplete scope with a stateless read path, locale-aware prefix retrieval, bounded typo tolerance, personalized ranking, and asynchronous index/cache refreshes.

findings.title: Stateless read path supports high-volume autocomplete
findings.explanation: The suggestion read API is explicitly stateless and composes cache, prefix index, profile features, and ranking through narrow calls, which is a good fit for large read-heavy workloads.

findings.title: Locale-aware indexing and caching for multilingual suggestions
findings.explanation: Locale is carried from the client through the read path and is used by the cache and prefix index, which directly supports multi-language autocomplete behavior.

findings.title: Asynchronous projection pipeline improves freshness without blocking reads
findings.explanation: Catalog changes and eligible interaction signals are buffered in an event stream and processed by projection workers, allowing real-time updates to propagate without delaying user-facing suggestion responses.

results.summary: A coherent distributed rate-limiter design with per-user/IP policy enforcement, tiered algorithms, atomic shared state, off-path telemetry, and explicit 429 guidance.

findings.title: Token-bucket default with policy-driven algorithm selection
findings.explanation: The learner explicitly chooses token bucket as the default while preserving other algorithms through versioned tier policy selection. This is a coherent fit for compact state, burst tolerance, and sustained-rate enforcement.

findings.title: Shared Redis state and atomic update path
findings.explanation: The design routes all admit/deny decisions through an authoritative shared Redis state with atomic check-and-update semantics, which directly supports distributed correctness and avoids instance-affinity dependence.

findings.title: Asynchronous telemetry keeps observability off the request path
findings.explanation: Breach and health signals are buffered in a queue and aggregated downstream, so monitoring and alerting do not add synchronous latency to the limiter decision path.

results.summary: The design coherently covers ingestion, real-time aggregation, query, alerting, dashboards, and tiered historical storage for high-volume distributed metrics.

findings.title: Type-aware metric handling is preserved end to end
findings.explanation: Counters, gauges, and histograms are treated as distinct metric families rather than flattened into a single sample model, which protects aggregation correctness.

findings.title: Tiered storage supports both hot queries and historical access
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates recent query-serving data from long-term archived blocks, which matches the mixed latency and retention needs of the brief.

results.summary: A Kafka-like distributed stream platform is designed with partitioned append-only storage, replication, leader fencing, replayable offsets, real-time processing, and monitoring, and it aligns closely with the published core scope.

findings.title: No material core gaps identified
findings.explanation: The submission covers publish/subscribe, durable replicated storage, real-time processing, ordering within partition, replay, graceful failure handling, horizontal scale, low latency, 1 MB messages, partition fencing, and at-least-once/exactly-once options in a coherent architecture.

results.summary: A coherent distributed key-value design with partition-aware routing, quorum-style consistency controls, durable storage, automatic repair, and a separately projected range index.

findings.title: Clear separation of base store and asynchronous range index
findings.explanation: The design keeps point-key correctness in the primary replica set while using an ordered secondary index for bounded range access. That separation fits the mixed workload without conflating the authoritative write path with the query-optimized path.

findings.title: Membership-driven routing and repair are coherently connected
findings.explanation: Gossip ownership epochs feed both coordinators and repair workers, which gives a consistent story for request routing, failure detection, and post-failure reconciliation.

findings.title: Durability path is explicitly layered
findings.explanation: The base store acknowledges durability, then emits committed mutations into a replayable change log for index projection and replica repair. That layered approach improves recovery clarity and reduces ambiguity about what is authoritative.

results.summary: The design is a coherent distributed crawler with durable host-sharded scheduling, robots/politeness enforcement, dedupe, retry handling, dynamic content support, and efficient storage for billion-scale crawling.

findings.title: Host-sharded frontier and fenced ownership provide strong crawl-scale control
findings.explanation: The frontier stores host-owned tasks with priority, due time, attempt state, and fenced lease metadata, while the router assigns hosts via consistent hashing and ownership epochs. This is a solid fit for billion-URL crawling because it bounds per-worker state and avoids hot-host split-brain.

findings.title: Robots and politeness are enforced before fetch/render execution
findings.explanation: The design keeps policy evaluation separate from permission to fetch, and both static fetches and browser rendering must obtain a shared host lease. That separation reduces the risk of violating crawl-delay or request-rate guidance under concurrent load.

findings.title: Duplicate detection combines fast hints with exact registry confirmation
findings.explanation: Bloom membership is treated only as a hint, while the registry stores canonical identities and exact content digests for confirmation. This balances throughput with safety against false positives.
